# Can a different ordering restore a feasible precision floor?

The logistic study found that even with all outcome labels, Portugal's course prefixes permitted at most 102 captures against a floor of 104. This development follow-up tests estimator dependence on the same, previously inspected data. Replace only the predictor with CatBoost using the identical admission or registration covariates, 300 iterations, depth 4, step size .05, seed 1701, one GPU. Use all training rows for the point model and the exact same forty bootstrap training index vectors as the logistic study for robust ranking. No tuning. Compare all nine policies, using the same boosted scores and fixed 10% course budgets. Record probability log loss and ROC AUC overall and by recorded group for both estimators. Test feasibility with the boosted unrestricted precision floor as well as the original absolute capture requirement. Include the full feasible option tables, candidate masks compressed as per-course group counts, validation against discrete and continuous formulations, and the same practical and precision criteria. A label-informed bound is an analysis of feasibility only. Reusing these cohorts limits claims to development.
